solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drunk returned drink — even shot (4-2)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back the way it came, so the word is read in reverse

annotation.surface: A drunk sends a drink back, a wild shot at the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface splits after 'drink'; the dash marks where the wordplay ends and the definition starts.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a fifty-fifty chance, as with the toss of a coin.

entries.clue: Playwright — everyone else better then? (6)

blocks.note: an American dramatist of the 1920s to 1950s, with an Irish surname
split 3+3: a number and a word for sick, the state in which the rest are well

annotation.surface: A rival sneers at a playwright, asking whether everyone else is better.
annotation.walkthrough: Split O'NEILL as ONE ILL: if only one person is ill, everyone else is better, in the sense of recovered, not superior.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Eugene O'Neill wrote Long Day's Journey into Night.

entries.clue: Old fighter reportedly happy, on having bagged record (5,6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is said aloud, so the words are spelt from their sound
indicatorNotes.having bagged: to bag something is to put it in a bag, so the outer pair holds the next piece inside

blocks.note: sunny = happy; SONNY is said the same way

annotation.surface: An old boxer, cheerful and fighting on, has another win on his record.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone covers 'happy, on' together, and the record goes inside between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Sonny Liston was a heavyweight boxing champion of the early 1960s.

entries.clue: Bird not entirely free, first two released from cage (9)

indicatorNotes.released from: what is released from a cage is let out of it, so those letters leave the word

annotation.surface: A caged bird is half let out, the door opened a little.
annotation.walkthrough: PART RID reads as 'partly rid', which is 'not entirely free'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a plump game bird shot in Britain from September.

entries.clue: Prove ineffective, as would Shackleton’s Endurance ultimately? (3,2,3)

blocks.note: an idiom for making no impression on someone
the ship could not break a way through the frozen sea

annotation.surface: A note on Shackleton's ship, whose efforts came to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Endurance was Shackleton's ship, trapped and finally crushed by Antarctic pack ice in 1915; read literally, it cut no ice.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an argument that cuts no ice makes no impression, the second sense taking it literally.

entries.clue: Tomahawk for Chinook, say? (7)

blocks.note: a tomahawk is a small axe, a tool for chopping
the Chinook is a twin-rotor military helicopter; 'say' marks an example

annotation.surface: A swap of one weapon for another, or of one tribe's name for another's.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like Native American terms, but both also name military hardware: the Tomahawk a missile, the Chinook a helicopter.
annotation.definitionFit: Two slang senses: an axe, and a helicopter, from its chopping rotor.

entries.clue: Fine material poet served up (5)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word is reversed

annotation.surface: A poet dishes up some fine cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Served up' suggests food on a plate; in a down clue it turns the poet's name upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: toile is a fine linen or cotton fabric, as in toile de Jouy.

entries.clue: Rotten part of climbing scaffold (3)

indicatorNotes.part of: a part of a word is some of its letters, so the answer is inside it
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing goes upward, so the letters read in reverse

annotation.surface: Some of the scaffolding being climbed has gone rotten.
annotation.walkthrough: The three letters sit in the middle of 'scaffold', read from bottom to top.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: milk or meat said to be off has spoiled.

entries.clue: Socialist leader crushed by Conservative country and American people (8)

indicatorNotes.crushed by: what is crushed lies beneath, so in a down clue it comes after the other pieces

annotation.surface: A left-wing leader is flattened by right-wing rule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Socialist leader' suggests a first letter S; it is Che Guevara, placed beneath C and OMAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Plains.

entries.clue: A loner wasted money from recording artist (8)

indicatorNotes.wasted: something wasted is ruined, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.from recording: what comes from a recording is heard, so the word is spelt from its sound

blocks.note: dough is money; the musical note DO is said the same way

annotation.surface: A solitary musician squanders his royalties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recording artist' reads as one phrase, but the break comes after 'recording': the definition is just 'artist'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Leonardo da Vinci, the Renaissance painter.

entries.clue: Disgrace taking my place, we hear? (6)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is sound, so the answer is spelt from how the phrase is said

annotation.surface: Someone takes my job and it feels like a disgrace.
annotation.walkthrough: It echoes the Carry On Cleo line 'Infamy, infamy, they've all got it in for me!'
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: notoriety, being widely known for something shameful.

entries.clue: Skin on rump of animals for butcher (6)

indicatorNotes.rump of: a rump is the hind end, so the last letter of the word
indicatorNotes.on: on means placed against, so the skin sits next to the S

blocks.note: a skin is an outer layer

annotation.surface: A butcher's cut: the hide still on an animal's rump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' suggests the meat trade, and the surface plays along; here it is a noun for a brutal killer.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a butcher is someone who kills savagely.

entries.clue: Keen stud would be at home here? (8)

annotation.definition2: stud would be at home here?

blocks.note: keen as in a sharp wind or a penetrating gaze

blocks.clueFragment: stud would be at home here?
blocks.note: a stud is a small earring, which sits in a hole made through the ear

annotation.surface: An eager stallion finds a home at a stud farm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stud' suggests a breeding horse; it is a small earring, whose home is a pierced hole.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: sharp or penetrating, and the hole made for jewellery.

entries.clue: Think about criminal model (11)

annotation.surface: Mulling over a crook who became a model.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container indicator; it belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ponder or consider something at length.

entries.clue: Asian leader once in magazine introduced to Asian daughter, Hello! (6,6)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the magazine sits within what follows
indicatorNotes.introduced to: to be introduced into something is to be put inside it

blocks.note: a rag is a cheap magazine or paper
from India; this is the clue's second 'Asian'

annotation.surface: A former Asian leader, featured in a magazine, is introduced to a daughter with a cheery hello.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Asian' appears twice: the first is part of the definition, the second becomes INDIAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister of India.

entries.clue: Money racket lands leader of opposition in jug (5,4)

indicatorNotes.lands: to land a fish is to catch and hold it, so BAT takes the O inside
indicatorNotes.leader of: a leader goes first, so the first letter of the word

blocks.note: a bat is a racket, as in table tennis

annotation.surface: A political scandal: a money racket puts the opposition leader in jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jug' is slang for jail, which suits the surface; here it is a jug for gravy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the boat-shaped jug that gravy is poured from.

entries.clue: Hike with it over ridge (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

annotation.surface: A walk with a companion over a ridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hike' pretends to be a walk; it is a rise, as in a price hike.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, in the sense of a price hike: a rise.

entries.clue: Lords according to Commons, say, befuddling paternal echo! (7,5)

indicatorNotes.befuddling: befuddling means confusing, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: Parliamentary tradition, repeated father to son, leaves everyone muddled.
annotation.walkthrough: By convention, MPs in the House of Commons refer to the House of Lords not by name but as 'another place'.
annotation.definitionFit: A parliamentary convention: the phrase MPs use for the other chamber.

entries.clue: Chicken soup cooked wrong (7)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Chicken soup made badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chicken soup' reads as a dish; the definition is only 'Chicken', and 'soup' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a chicken killed young, from the French for chick.

entries.clue: Soldiers after deal for shooter? (6)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so below in a down clue

blocks.note: to mete out is to deal out

annotation.surface: Soldiers after an arms deal for a gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' suggests a gun; it is a shooting star.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a shooting star, so something that shoots across the sky.

entries.clue: Two kings first to uncork fine wine (5,3)

indicatorNotes.first to: the first to arrive leads, so the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: Two kings, the first to open a bottle of fine wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The two kings are spelt as their royal cyphers, with the AND between them kept.
annotation.definitionFit: A French wine term: the top classification of vineyard, and its wine.

entries.clue: Oxygen fed to just over three hundred bacteria (5)

indicatorNotes.fed to: what is fed to something goes into it, so the O goes inside

blocks.note: O is the symbol for oxygen

annotation.surface: Bacteria given oxygen, a little over three hundred of them.
annotation.walkthrough: Just over three hundred is 301; the oxygen goes after its first C.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the round-celled bacteria, as in streptococci.

entries.clue: Delegate with foot rolled over puppy? (6)

indicatorNotes.rolled over: something rolled over is turned the other way, so read backwards

blocks.note: to foot the bill is to pay it

annotation.surface: A puppy rolls over at a delegate's foot.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'puppy' defines by example: a small dog, forever barking.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition by example: a young dog that never stops barking.

entries.clue: Main course in Pakistan, cold (6)

blocks.note: a balti is a curry, named from a word for bucket
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A main course in Pakistan, served cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main course' reads as one phrase; 'Main' alone is the sea, an old word for the open ocean.
annotation.definitionFit: A poetic sense: the main is the open sea, and this is a northern European sea.

entries.clue: Seen empty, food container (3)

blocks.note: SEEN with its middle removed leaves SN, a chemical symbol

annotation.surface: An empty food tin has been spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: Emptying SEEN leaves SN, and Sn is tin's symbol in the periodic table.
annotation.definitionFit: A British plain synonym: a can of food, and Sn is the element's symbol.

entries.clue: Appear to smuggle whiskey into school, for example (4,1,3)

indicatorNotes.to smuggle: to smuggle something is to hide it inside, so the W goes within
indicatorNotes.into: into means going inside the next word

annotation.surface: A pupil tries to smuggle whiskey into school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' is a shoal of fish, not a classroom.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the old naval wake-up call means get out of bed, so turn up.

entries.clue: Model goes in to fill centre of banner for advertiser (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Model: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped
indicatorNotes.to fill: what fills something sits inside it, so the anagram goes between the two Ns

annotation.surface: A model steps in to fill the middle of a poster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun, the person on the banner; it is a verb, reshaping GOES IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a glowing sign that advertises a shop or bar.

entries.clue: Hypothesis way removed from the narrative (6)

indicatorNotes.removed from: removed from means taken out of, so ST is deleted from what follows

annotation.surface: A hypothesis takes a detour away from the story.
annotation.walkthrough: The way is ST, the abbreviation for street, taken out of THE STORY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a proposed explanation not yet proven.
